text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — streaming-gateway-usw2: error-rate(5xx) spike. Current 5xx ~7.8% over last 3m (baseline 0.3%). Multiple partial stream closes and client cancels. Paging oncall. thread_ts=2351234567

maya: oncall dave, you up? seeing timeouts and chunked body truncation in prod logs. customers reporting partial responses.

dave_oncall: I'm on it. pinging SRE team. any red metrics for e2e latency?

jeremy: yes — tail latency P99 for streaming increased from 140ms -> 2.2s. gateway upstream returns lots of 502/504 and some 500s with body: "chunked: premature end of stream".

kevin: copying logs: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] gw|conn=1245|req=ctx-9a3|status=502|err="chunked: unexpected EOF"
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] svc-model|tok=abcd|status=200|client_disconnect=true
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] gw|conn=1246|req=ctx-9a4|status=504|err="upstream timeout"
```

carol: customer-impact: support case #8472 (Acme Corp) reports truncated chat responses during the spike. estimated affected requests ~4k in last 10m.

ingrid: quick triage — looks like an increase in client cancel rates (499) followed by gateway 5xx for the same flow. Could be buffering/backpressure issue on streaming path.

maya: good call. could be the gateway's streaming proxy limits (max chunk size or idle window). Any recent deploys?

dave_oncall: No prod deploys in last 2h per deploy-bot. infra autoscale events at 13:58UTC. I will push temporary routing change: divert new streaming sessions to standby pool in eu-west while we investigate.

jeremy: before that, can we turn on extra logging for the chunked decoder? Add header X-Debug-Stream: true and sample 1% of traffic. Command: ```kubectl exec -it gw-pod-0 -- curl -X PATCH http://localhost:9000/debug -d '{"stream_logging":true}'``` (run in prod cluster).

kevin: I can do the debug patch and bump gateway replicas by +3 on the cluster to relieve load. running now.

carol: notify support + account team for Acme. send a short status note: "we're investigating partial responses, mitigation in progress — more updates in 15m".

incident-bot: Escalation step: internal pager group alerted, ops channel created #incident-2351234567. Severity set to Sev2.

dave_oncall: Done. Enabling fallback to non-streaming paged responses for VIP customers (Acme) to avoid partial payloads. Patch config: ```
route: /v1/streaming -> fallback: /v1/paged?sync=true
headers: set X-Stream-Fallback: forced
``` Applying for tenant Acme only.

maya: Good. That should reduce customer impact while we root-cause. How long to roll?

dave_oncall: Target 2 minutes. rolling flags via ff-service now.

jeremy: Observed immediate drop in active streaming connections routed through the troubled gateway by 60%. 5xx rate dropped to 3.1% in the next 2m but still higher than baseline.

kevin: After replica bump and routing change, CPU on gw nodes down from 92% -> 58%. chunked EOF errors still appear but less frequent. I'm collecting tcpdump from a few pods for offline analysis.

ingrid: Hypothesis: long-lived client cancellations are leaving partial state in the gateway's streaming buffer; combined with a recent kernel update on hosts that changed TCP keepalive defaults, causing earlier FIN behavior.

carol: Can we toggle keepalive back to the previous values as a test? We should be careful — do in canary first.

dave_oncall: Will flip host sysctl on 2 canary nodes: net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time from 600 -> 120. Applying now to gw-canary-1, gw-canary-2. Monitoring.

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff planned at +60m unless incident resolved. Next update scheduled in 15m.

maya: Support page updated. Assigned follow-ups: - kevin to collect pcaps and system metrics - jeremy to correlate proxy logs with model service logs - ingrid to verify kernel and package changes across hosts - dave to coordinate routing and feature flags.

carol: Recorded customer impact summary: partial/short responses for ~0.6% of total traffic during window; high-profile customer Acme impacted — ticket created.

kevin: pcaps and extra logs pushed to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2351234567/ — link: https://s3.example/2351234567/ (internal).

jeremy: follow-up: I see a pattern where fast client cancels (sub-200ms) leave upstream in-flight tokens that model service treats as canceled, but gateway still streaming chunk footer and then hits conn reset -> chunked decode error. We'll instrument per-request lifecycle to confirm.

dave_oncall: TL;DR: mitigation in place (fallback for VIPs, extra replicas, keepalive canary). Customer-impact reduced. Next steps: full host sysctl rollback if canary looks good, deeper postmortem on streaming proxy buffer handling, add robust cancellation propagation test in CI.

maya: Thanks team. Will keep channel open for status. if anyone sees regression ping @dave_oncall. :thumbsup:
